ablation.note: rules only is the deterministic detector verdict, held for 300 seconds against both endpoints of the flow it named. the hold matters: a rule raises one alert per episode and then goes quiet on its own cooldown, so scoring the bare fire against every row would report a recall near zero for a detector that in fact caught the attack. model only is the argmax of the calibrated tier-1 probability on its own. both is what the engine actually does, which is to let a held rule name the class and to let the model name a class alone only when it clears model_alert_confidence and the benign-only isolation forest also calls the row unusual. one artefact of holding the verdict against both endpoints is worth naming: a dns rule that names a host and its resolver marks the resolver too, so every other host querying that resolver in the next window counts as a rules positive and the rules-only precision for the dns class is understated by that spill
